# Emergence integration record

Upstream: Meta_Kim by KimYx0207, https://github.com/KimYx0207/Meta_Kim

Version: 3.7.3 from the user-supplied Meta_Kim-main.zip.
Archive SHA-256: 27932415b4ac078f51fcff92ea38094c8d222960e475701e6a1c7a6df32a99f0.

2026-10-30: Emergence extracted nine governance role responsibility/boundary records and eight-stage workflow contracts into a validated built-in catalog. Chinese labels and a non-exclusive mapping from the eleven business phases to related core stages were added by Emergence. The mapping is an integration interpretation, not an upstream execution graph.

The 16 source files under this directory retain their original bytes. LICENSE and NOTICE apply to those sources and derived catalog data. No upstream executable module, hook, installer, or SKILL entry point is run or registered. The observer, Harness adapter, diagnostic storage and Chinese inspection surface are Emergence implementations. The catalog does not grant execution authority or inject upstream instructions into model requests.

Source hashes for every file in the archive, category routing, maturity limitations and migration dispositions are recorded in the workspace document docs/meta-kim-source-inventory.json. The runtime catalog contains hashes for the preserved sources. Reproduce the catalog with scripts/import-meta-kim.py and the exact pinned archive; the importer rejects a different archive hash.

No endorsement or runtime certification by the upstream author is implied. Upstream test/status declarations have not been converted into Emergence live-validation claims.

2026-10-30, integration phase 6: Emergence added full lifecycle acceptance, actual Harness compaction and MCP timeout tests, current-build off/observe overhead measurement, and explicit configured-provider checks. Acceptance exposed and fixed loss of local execution identity when creating a repair attempt in Emergence's scheduler. These checks validate Emergence implementations, not the complete upstream runtime. Optional external services remain unconfigured on the tested machine; preserved upstream sources remain unchanged.

2026-10-30, integration phase 5: Emergence added independent review/verification tasks with host-recorded evidence and bounded checks, plus session/project/personal memory candidates, human approval, revision, rollback and forgetting. Short Prism/Warden/Sentinel and Librarian/Chrysalis responsibility extracts from the validated catalog guide these boundaries. Executable policy changes are not applied through memory. External Graphify and memory services remain optional MCP integrations, not automatically synchronized or certified. The preserved upstream source files are unchanged.

2026-10-30, integration phase 4: Emergence implemented plan submission into its existing Collaboration scheduler, a SQLite execution journal with OS ownership and fencing, bounded side-effect observations, explicit recovery decisions, and inherited permission constraints for new attempts. These are Emergence implementations of the studied execution/recovery boundaries, not an import or certification of upstream runtime modules. External side effects are not promised exactly-once. The 16 preserved upstream source files remain unchanged.

2026-10-30, integration phase 3: Emergence added its own bounded task-plan schema, live Harness capability adapter, session-local plan storage and restrictive planning gate. Short responsibility extracts for Conductor, Scout and Artisan from the validated catalog now inform complex-task planning. This supersedes the phase-2 statement that no catalog-derived guidance enters model requests; it does not import full upstream prompts, run upstream code or grant execution authority. All 16 preserved source files remain byte-identical. Existing Emergence permissions and collaboration scheduling remain authoritative.
